correctness.rationale: A direct rooted-forest determinant proves the known full cyclic-set law. Telescoping gives the tail moments and exact two-point covariance. The bundled exact rational checker verifies strict signs for n=2..168 and exhaustive maps through n=6, while a Gaussian integral upper bound and explicit rational comparisons prove all n>=169. Increasing Boolean functions on at most two coordinates yield an exhaustive n<=3 negative-association test. Positive covariance of disjoint two-coordinate AND events for n=4,5 and individual indicators for n>=6 completes necessity. The limit follows by controlled Riemann sums. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full cyclic-set and cyclic-count distribution are acknowledged as classical (Pitman 2001 and Hansen–Jaworski 2006). Published-index and primary-literature comparisons did not identify the sharp all-size three-phase classification of negative association, positive disjoint pair-event covariance, and pairwise sign inversion. This is a structural refinement requiring new nontrivial global inequalities, not a new distribution formula. Historical implicit coverage is an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: Cycle membership is a canonical exchangeable random subset of a functional digraph. Negative association implies broad covariance and concentration properties for disjoint increasing observables, so the first failure at four vertices is structurally meaningful. The negative-pairwise but positive-disjoint-event window at n=4,5 distinguishes genuine negative association from pairwise tests, while the all-size n=6 positive switch and limiting rescaled covariance show a sustained phase transition. The precise size thresholds are natural and not arbitrary computation slices.
